In every book of machines and used now and then to drain building pits and ditches; mines prefer piston pumps and bucket chains.
- **Gears and gear trains** [`gears_gear_trains`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gears_gear_trains.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Millwrights build wooden cog and lantern gearing, clockmakers cut brass wheels, increasingly on dividing engines. Tooth shape is by eye; no theory is in print. Local: millwrights; Vienna clockmakers. Elsewhere: London and Paris: wheel-cutting engines.

Locksmiths, gunsmiths and instrument makers cut screws with plates and taps, each workshop to its own thread. A nut fits only its own bolt. Local: gunsmiths and locksmiths; arsenal workshops.

Water-driven leather and wooden box bellows blow the furnaces and forges of Styria. The Chinese double-acting piston box is unknown. Local: ironworks at the Styrian Erzberg.

- **Sand and loam moulding for large castings** [`sand_loam_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sand_loam_casting.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Bronze guns, mortars and bells are cast in loam over a core. Iron is cast only as shot, bombs, stove plates; nobody casts iron thin or to size. Local: imperial gun founders (Stückgießer); imperial and civic arsenals; bell founders.

- **Rolling and slitting mill** [`rolling_mill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rolling_mill.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Mints roll coin strip, the Hall mint even strikes between engraved rollers; glaziers roll window lead. Bar iron is hammered, not rolled or slit, in the Austrian works. Local: Vienna mint; mint at Hall in Tyrol (roller coining since c. 1567–1571). Elsewhere: Liège region and England: slitting mills for nail rod.
- **Precision cylinder boring** [`boring_machine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boring_machine.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Guns are cast hollow and reamed smooth by horse or water power; the bore follows the casting and is neither straight nor round to a steam engine's needs. Local: imperial gun foundry and arsenal.
- **Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest** [`lathe_screw_cutting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lathe_screw_cutting.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept high. Turners work wood, ivory and brass on pole and wheel lathes with hand-held tools; Besson's screw lathe is a picture in a book. No slide rest, no lead screw. Local: turners (Drechsler); clock and instrument makers.
- **Precision measurement (flat surfaces, gauges, micrometer)** [`precision_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/precision_measurement.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Instrument makers divide scales with transversals; the vernier is in books. Workshops fit part to part by eye and file. Gunners gauge shot with ring calibres. Local: arsenal shot gauges; mint weights and assay balances. Elsewhere: Paris Observatory: screw micrometer and telescopic sights (Auzout, Picard).

- **Interchangeable parts** [`interchangeable_parts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interchangeable_parts.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Shot is cast to calibre, but imperial guns come in many calibres and every musket lock is fitted by hand. Guild masters see gauges as an insult to skill. Local: imperial arsenal; gunsmiths.
- **Assembly line and mass production** [`assembly_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/assembly_line.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Guild rules limit journeymen per master and forbid mixing trades. Becher's state 'Kunst- und Werkhaus' on the Tabor tried large workshops; the guilds fought it. Local: Becher's Werkhaus on the Tabor (burned in the 1683 war); arsenal workshops, outside guild control. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal; France: Colbert's royal manufactories.

Water-driven Italian silk-throwing mills are known; Becher's Werkhaus had a silk manufactory. Wool and flax are spun by hand in cottages; spinners' wages are what the poor live on. Elsewhere: Bologna and Piedmont: silk-throwing mills.

- **Flying shuttle and power loom** [`power_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/power_loom.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. The ribbon 'mill' loom weaving many ribbons at once is known and hated; German towns forbid it; an imperial ban follows in 1685. Ribbon and trimming makers (Posamentierer) would riot. Elsewhere: Leiden, Danzig, Basel: ribbon engine looms.

- **Stocking frame (knitting machine)** [`knitting_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/knitting_frame.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Elsewhere: London and Nottinghamshire: framework knitters; France: frames since Colbert's time.
